_comment: PID polyglot conformance fixture (doc 25). The producer is TypeScript
(game-server) and the verifier is Rust (commit-service); they are joined
ONLY by these bytes, so a change to either side's MAC input must red the
`raw` is the EXACT proposal payload as XADDed. It is signed as BYTES and
never re-serialised (PID-D2), which is why there is no canonical-JSON
rule here to get wrong: serde_json and JSON.stringify never have to agree
on key order, spacing or number formatting.
If this ever needs regenerating, regenerate from ONE side and let the
other side's test fail first. A fixture rewritten from both at once
proves only that both were changed.
